description.en: The Common poorwill is a highly specialized, nocturnal nightjar native to the arid and semi-arid landscapes of western North America. It holds the unique distinction of being the only bird species known to enter a state of extended torpor—effectively hibernating—to survive harsh winter conditions when its insect prey is scarce.
description.zh: 弱夜鹰是一种高度特化的夜行性夜鹰，原产于北美洲西部的干旱和半干旱景观。它拥有一个独特的生物学地位：这是已知唯一一种能够进入长期蛰伏状态（实际上相当于冬眠）的鸟类，以此在昆虫猎物稀缺的严冬中存活下来。

anatomy.en: Measuring merely 18-21 cm in length, it is the smallest North American nightjar. Its plumage is a masterclass in cryptic camouflage, featuring intricate mottling of silver-gray, black, and warm brown that renders it virtually invisible against rocky substrates and leaf litter. It possesses a disproportionately large head, a diminutive bill that opens into a cavernous, bristle-fringed gape adapted for aerial insect capture, and relatively short, rounded wings compared to other caprimulgids.
anatomy.zh: 体长仅18-21厘米，是北美洲体型最小的夜鹰。它的羽毛是隐蔽伪装的杰作，银灰色、黑色和暖棕色的复杂斑驳图案使其在岩石基质和落叶层中几乎隐形。它拥有不成比例的大头部，喙虽小但张开后形成一个边缘长满刚毛的巨大口裂，极度适应空中捕食昆虫；与其他夜鹰科鸟类相比，其翅膀较短且呈圆形。

ecology_and_behavior.en: Strictly nocturnal and crepuscular, the Common poorwill hunts by sallying forth from the ground to catch moths, beetles, and other flying insects. Its most extraordinary physiological adaptation is its capacity for profound torpor. During winter or periods of extreme environmental stress, it can lower its metabolic rate drastically, dropping its body temperature to as low as 4.3°C (39.7°F) and remaining inactive for weeks or even months, hidden in shallow rock crevices.
ecology_and_behavior.zh: 弱夜鹰严格遵循夜行性和晨昏性活动规律，通过从地面突然起飞来捕食飞蛾、甲虫和其他飞行昆虫。其最非凡的生理适应能力是深度蛰伏。在冬季或极端环境压力时期，它可以大幅降低代谢率，将体温降至极低的4.3°C（39.7°F），并隐藏在浅岩石缝隙中数周甚至数月保持不活动状态。

habitat_and_distribution.en: This species is intrinsically linked to dry, open habitats including sagebrush steppes, chaparral, rocky canyons, and desert scrublands. Its breeding range extends from the arid interior of southern British Columbia and Alberta, south through the western United States, reaching as far as central and southern Mexico. It requires areas with sparse vegetation and exposed gravel or rock for roosting and nesting.
habitat_and_distribution.zh: 该物种与干旱、开阔的栖息地有着内在的联系，包括三齿蒿草原、查帕拉尔灌丛、多岩石的峡谷和沙漠灌木丛。其繁殖范围从不列颠哥伦比亚省和阿尔伯塔省南部的干旱内陆延伸，向南穿过美国西部，一直到达墨西哥中南部。它需要植被稀疏且有裸露砾石或岩石的区域来进行栖息和筑巢。

habitat.text_en: Arid and semi-arid scrublands, sagebrush steppes, and rocky canyons across western North America.
habitat.text_zh: 遍布北美洲西部的干旱和半干旱灌木丛、三齿蒿草原以及多岩石的峡谷。
